Chilli thrips
Scirtothrips dorsalis (Family Thripidae)
Description:
Eggs: Pale yellow, kidney shaped and inserted into leaf tissue (not
normally seen).
Immatures: Pale yellow, similar shape to adult. Size: up to 0.8 mm.
Adults: Pale yellow with dark antennae, dark stripes on the back of
the lower abdomen and dark feathery wings. They are very active.
Size: 0.8 mm in length.
Life Cycle: Development from egg to adult takes up to 21 days.
Similar to: Other pale coloured thrips.
Damage: Adults and nymphs feed by rasping and sucking sap from
soft flush leaves. The damage can be seen as brown scarring on the
leaves.
Other Comments: These thrips have been noticed on flush leaves
on the occasional mango tree in the Darwin rural and Katherine areas.
This damage is very similar to redbanded thrips damage.
Monitoring: Check the upper surface of young leaves for nymphs
and adults.

It is included as a supplementary international reference for visual identification and general pest/disease biology only. Species presence, seasonal timing (the guide's monthly monitoring calendars reflect the NT dry/wet season cycle), and any pesticide or chemical guidance are specific to northern Australia and may not apply directly to Cambodian conditions, seasons, or registered products. This edition of the source itself does not list specific pesticide products or rates (noted as intentionally omitted pending updated registrations), so none are reported here either.
